may_be_looking_for: People with a certain number of CD19-positive B cells in their blood
People who have had previous B-cell targeted therapy and whose B cell counts have returned to normal or higher
People with adequate blood counts (e.g., absolute neutrophil count at least 1.5×10⁹/L, hemoglobin at least 80 g/L, platelet count at least 50×10⁹/L for certain conditions)
People with adequate organ function (liver, kidney, lung, heart)
may_exclude_people_who: Do not voluntarily sign informed consent or cannot complete study procedures
Have blood counts or organ function below the required thresholds
Have not recovered from previous B-cell therapy (B cell counts not returned to normal)
Have other medical conditions that could interfere with the study
patient_summary: This pilot study is testing a type of cell therapy called anti-CD19/BCMA-UCAR-T cells in people with certain autoimmune diseases. The study will enroll about 36 to 72 participants.
patient_title: Study of Anti-CD19/BCMA CAR-T Cells for Autoimmune Diseases
questions_to_ask_clinician: What are the potential benefits and risks of this CAR-T cell therapy?
How does this study differ from standard treatments for my autoimmune disease?
What is the process of receiving the anti-CD19/BCMA-UCAR-T cells, including the lymphodepleting chemotherapy?
What follow-up tests and visits will be required if I participate?
Are there any alternative treatment options available?
uncertainty_notes: This is an early-stage pilot study, so there is limited information about the safety and study outcomes of this therapy. Results will help guide future research.
The study is enrolling in China only, which may affect generalizability to other populations.
The phase of the study is listed as N/A, indicating it may not fit standard phases.
what_researchers_are_studying: Researchers are studying whether anti-CD19/BCMA-UCAR-T cells can be safe and associated with the study outcome for treating autoimmune diseases such as dermatomyositis, rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, and systemic sclerosis.
